children: Janus Electric Holdings
is proposing a $15 million placement with an option to increase the raising to $20m as it seeks to expand its electric truck conversion capacity to meet growing demand.
The heavy vehicle electrification specialist has contracted 124 truck conversions across North America with an indicative gross value of approximately $90m, including 99 vehicles in the US.
Its first US truck conversion for Ability Tri-Modal at the Port of Los Angeles is undergoing final commissioning and is targeted to enter service this week.

Janus believes its ability to convert, fund, and deliver trucks has become the principal constraint on growth as its combined order book and sales pipeline across the US, Canada, and Australia reaches 797 vehicles with an estimated value of $538m.
North American Expansion
The US accounts for approximately $64.6m of contracted orders, with the Canadian component comprising 25 conversions for an Ontario consortium valued at approximately $25m.

Beyond those contracts, Janus is pursuing proposals, pilot projects, and verbal extensions covering 241 vehicles valued at approximately $157m across its three core markets, targeting decisions within around 90 days.
A further 432 vehicles representing an estimated $291m sit in potential follow-on programs dependent on the progress of pilot projects.
The company has identified additional opportunities covering 380 vehicles worth approximately $271m outside its three core markets.
US Delivery Incentives
Janus is targeting up to 18 US trucks on the road by 31 December, and plans to increase output to 50 conversion kits a month in the third quarter of the 2027 financial year.
The company has identified approximately A$36.5m (US$23.7m) in potential incentives across 104 trucks as US funding opportunities expand.
California’s truck voucher program is expected to reopen around 15 December with A$208.5m (US$135.5m) in funding and an increase in the per-fleet voucher limit from 20 to 50 vehicles.
Janus has lodged voucher applications covering 25 trucks and expects the higher fleet limit to make another 75 vehicles eligible for funding.
Larger Operating Footprint

The proposed placement would allocate $6m to establishing a permanent US operating base and developing cloud and software infrastructure, alongside $4m in initial funding for battery and charging services.
Further expenditure would support Australian leased truck deployments, demonstration, and lease vehicles across all three markets, US sales, and operations and expansion of the ConGlobal initiative.
Any additional $5m raised under the placement upsize option would be directed towards the battery and charging services business, with the board retaining discretion over allocations.
Janus plans to supplement the raising with its existing $11m financing facility, potential proceeds from options and warrants and customer incentives.
The company expects a December decision on its application to the Australian Renewable Energy Agency’s
Driving the Nation
program.

title: Janus Electric to Raise up to $20m for Truck Conversion Capacity Expansion
